name: Grid equivalent source
summary: A voltage source behind an impedance used in study diagrams to represent the external network at a defined fault level.
description: A grid equivalent source represents the upstream network in load flow, short circuit and stability studies as an ideal voltage source behind an impedance. The impedance is calculated from the declared fault level and X/R ratio at the connection point, often with separate maximum and minimum cases.

Study single-line diagrams draw it as a circle with a sine wave followed by an impedance element, labelled with the fault level in MVA or kA and the X/R ratio. Microgrid studies use it to test both strong and weak network conditions before islanding scenarios are modelled.

The equivalent is only valid near the declared fault level; it cannot represent upstream dynamics such as voltage control or frequency response unless additional models are attached. The symbol does not tell you which study case it belongs to.
readingNotes: Read both the fault level and X/R ratio.
Check whether the drawing shows maximum or minimum fault case.
drawingChecklist: State fault level, X/R ratio and voltage.
distinction: A grid equivalent is a study model; a utility grid connection symbol represents the real supply on construction drawings.
